title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
signature: minDays(bloomDay: List[int], m: int, k: int) -> int
statement: Flower i blooms on day bloomDay[i]. A bouquet needs k adjacent bloomed flowers, and each flower can be used once. Return the earliest day by which you can make m bouquets, or -1 if it is impossible.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(22)
    return [[r.randint(1, 10**9) for _ in range(100000)], 100, 100]

hints.1_question: If someone names a day, can you check how many bouquets are possible? Does the number of possible bouquets only grow as the day grows?
hints.2_nudge: Binary search the day. To count bouquets on a given day, scan left to right counting a run of bloomed flowers; every k in a row makes a bouquet and resets the run. An unbloomed flower breaks the run.
hints.3_big_hint: If m*k > len(bloomDay) return -1. Search lo = min, hi = max bloom day. ok(day): flowers = bouquets = 0; if b <= day: flowers += 1; if flowers == k: bouquets += 1; flowers = 0; else flowers = 0.

known_bugs.name: ignores adjacency (counts bloomed flowers // k)
known_bugs.followup: A bouquet needs k flowers next to each other. If one flower in a row hasn't bloomed, what happens to the run?

known_bugs.name: never returns -1
known_bugs.followup: What if there are fewer than m * k flowers in total? Can any day work?

known_bugs.name: run is not reset after completing a bouquet
known_bugs.followup: After a bouquet is made, those flowers are used up. What should the run length be for the next flower?

followups: Why is feasibility monotonic in the day number?
Why check m * k > n first?
